chapter: New Orleans clarinetists and learning the guitar
title: Lessons from Manuel Perez; his circle and Henry Morton's place
summary: Manuel as Freddie's friend; Henry Morton's place on Magazine; cousin Albert Warner and who should replace Pajeaud in the band.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: I know. Manuel Mineta teaches all of those same kind of things. Manuel Mineta? He teaches time like that, too, and all that.

I'm talking about Manuel. That is my brother's best friend, him and Freddie. He used to play violin. When Freddie was playing cornet, he used to be, and him and Freddie, every time you see Freddie, you see him. They used to go at this fellow, what they call Henry Morton. Henry Morton's place, they used to go up on Second and Magazine. Well, that was a fine place. Oh, it was a fine place. I don't know if you heard talk about this fellow here, what they call him again, this here fellow, I can't forget it, I can't, John Rucker. No? He was a good comedian. Well, them three used to be together. He was good. We used to play for him at the economy hall, you know. But he was fine. He was a good comedian. But talk about this man here, Manuel, I will, I ain't seen him since the time you brought him here. He came by here a year ago. And I sure was glad to see him. Of course, he didn't, he didn't fain away a little bit though, you know. Well, you see, my daddy was in the same boat as him. See, just like him and my daddy, same color, but of course he done got like a lemon, you know. So that's why I said, well, I said, well, we can't always be the same way all the time. But my daddy is a perfect position. From a piano, and what they call them things that works on them post there, the Calliope, eh?

Calliope, he can play that. Because I say, yeah. Well, he played with P. Roy and all of them. See? Now, of course, this fellow, yeah, they tell me, I ain't seen him yet. But I told my cousin Warnick that the old man will fit this Pajou's place will be Peter Bocard. And they tell me he's in the band.
Yeah, he's been playing with the Urican.
They tell me he's in the band.
Albert Warner is your, uh... That's my first cousin.

Your first cousin. Yeah. Well, he ain't been playing as long as me. No. Yeah, he come out with a horn. The bell must have been about that big. Old horn he had. And he started learning. And I believe Shalini learned him. I'd play a trampoline. So that's make, I says, well, I says, now, I said, Warnick, I say, Pajou's dead now, eh? I say, he said, yeah, I don't know who they got. I said, well, the best man would fit that would be, Charlie Love or Peter Bocard. Of course, I said, I don't say that they got a rag. Well, this fella here, he wasn't too much of a rag. He wasn't much of a ragtime man. He wasn't a jazz. Of course, this fella here, what they call like Brimfield and this other fella here, I forgot his name. Well, anyhow, them was good street mans, you know? But them mans, what I'm talking about, like Charlie Bocard, Charlie Love, this fella with Dodd here, Pajou. Well, them musicians, they got the stuff with them. Now, of course, I ain't put them like Howard and Clayton and all that. That's only street mans, you know? Of course, people, I understand people like to go for that. But you know, you never know who you're going to run across. Who you going to run across? Somebody going to condemn you someday. They're going to throw something against your face and say, you're a musician? Yeah, I am. Play that for me, please. And there, you're condemned. Well, we don't play that away. Well, then you can't call yourself a musician.
That's right. You can say you're doing the best you can. What was that place you were telling us about, a second of the magazine when Freddie and...
Martin? That was Henry and Morton. Now, they got there. I talk about Henry and Morton and Trump.
I'm done. I'm done. I'm done.
